name: Codequiry API
description:
Programmatic access to Codequiry. The typical flow is: create a check, upload one or more ZIP submissions, start the check, then poll status and read the overview / detailed results.

All endpoints are under the base URL `https://codequiry.com/api/v1` and authenticate with an `apikey` request header (your 64-character key from the dashboard). There is no OAuth and no Bearer token.

Many check-scoped operations expose two equivalent forms: a POST form that takes `check_id` in the body, and a RESTful form that takes the id in the URL (e.g. `POST /check/status` and `GET /checks/{checkId}/status`). They are interchangeable.

**Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute, counted per client IP address (not per API key) and shared across every endpoint. The limit is the same on all plans. Failed calls, including 401s, count against it. Over the limit the API returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

**Timestamps** are UTC strings formatted `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

**Polling:** analysis is asynchronous. After `POST /check/start`, poll `POST /check/status` until `status_id` is 4 (completed) or 3 (failed); results endpoints return 409 until then. Poll every 20-30 seconds — a tight loop will exhaust the rate limit long before a check finishes.

**Webhooks (instead of polling):** set `callback_url` when you create a check, or an account-wide webhook URL in Dashboard → API Keys, and Codequiry POSTs a JSON body to it when the check finishes:

```json
{
  "event": "check.completed",
  "check_id": 12345,
  "name": "Week 4 essays",
  "course_id": 678,
  "status_id": 4,
  "status": "Completed",
  "submissions_count": 30,
  "avg_peer_similarity": 12.4,
  "avg_web_similarity": 3.1,
  "results_url": "https://dashboard.codequiry.com/course/678/assignment/12345",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-31T12:00:00+00:00"
}
```

`event` is `check.completed` or `check.failed`. Each delivery carries `X-Codequiry-Event` and `X-Codequiry-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with your API key — verify it with a constant-time compare before trusting the payload, and reply 2xx to acknowledge. Delivery is best-effort and unauthenticated destinations are rejected: the URL must be public http(s), so loopback, private and link-local addresses are refused with 422 at create time.

**Errors** are always JSON, on every status, whether or not you send an `Accept` header. `error` carries the human-readable reason; 422 adds `validation_errors` keyed by field. A 402 means the account is suspended for an unpaid invoice and every endpoint will refuse until it is paid.
